---
title: Learning from community programming
description: A proposed evaluation agenda connecting local experience, program improvement, and policy questions.
---

::: {.status}

Evaluation approach proposed

:::


TSP’s community model should be able to learn from the people who use it. Before implementation, an evaluation plan needs to define useful questions, proportionate methods, consent and privacy arrangements, and how findings will be returned to communities.

## Questions worth planning for

- How did a gathering operate, and what adaptations were needed?
- Which practical access barriers did teens and facilitators encounter?
- What resources, relationships, and support did projects need?
- How did participants describe their role in decision-making?
- Which proposed activities were implemented, changed, or abandoned, and why?
- What outcomes could be examined responsibly, without overclaiming attribution?

## Use evaluation to improve the work

Implementation notes, facilitator reflections, voluntary feedback, and appropriately designed outcome measures could each answer different questions. They should not be collapsed into a single success score. Communities need room to describe setbacks and disagreement.

Local findings can suggest changes to guides and event design. Recurring barriers may also raise questions about compensation, access, and public support for service. Those connections can inform the broader research agenda without treating a small local sample as national evidence.

## Before collecting information

Establish who is responsible for data, what is necessary, consent and assent requirements, secure storage, access, retention, and whether independent ethical review is needed. Do not place participant records or identifiable quotations in this public repository.

No program evaluation data have been collected or findings published through this alpha. [See how communities can share nonidentifying feedback](../programs/feedback.qmd).
